status: Planned before Chronos-2 inference; earlier baseline and Chronos-Bolt results inspected. Exploratory follow-up, not an independent confirmation or a preregistration.
question: Does seasonal baseline choice also change the margin and uncertainty for Chronos-2, and how does Chronos-2 compare with Chronos-Bolt at matched history?
history: Same origin-inclusive up-to-2048-hour history as Bolt; Q1 shorter; NaN gaps retained; latest 336 hours complete. No interpolation or future observations.
inference: Zero-shot, target-only, float32, median (0.5 quantile); each origin a separate univariate task; cross_learning=False; context_length=2048; native horizon prediction.
selection: Frozen validation-MAE baseline rule and blend weight. No test-based reselection or tuning.
metrics: Reuse baseline_pilot.score for MAE, RMSE, MAPE; MAE primary. Per-case percentage gain undefined when comparator MAE is zero; no pooled raw-unit errors.
uncertainty: Reuse chronos_uncertainty.calendar_losses and paired_interval: origin-level horizon MAE, paired circular blocks, 5000 resamples, 168 and 336 calendar hours, 95% intervals, seed 20261019 plus first eight SHA256 hex digits of window/dataset/series/horizon plus block.
clear: Both block lengths favour the same method, with at least two blocks of valid origins at each length; otherwise unclear/block-sensitive or limited_data.
meaningful: Clear and at least 5% lower MAE; 2% and 10% sensitivity, as in the Bolt comparison.
reporting: Report all cases including Portugal T3 zero-error baselines; Q1 separately because history is shorter. Count weakened and strengthened clear wins vs weekly/selected for each model. Include paired Chronos-2 vs Bolt intervals, with positive favouring Chronos-2.
limits: No multiplicity correction. Short windows, related meters, Q4 repeats pilot, household sparse, cases already inspected, pretraining overlap not ruled out. Two models from the same family do not establish cross-family generality.
